governing_statute.value: Conn. Gen. Stat. chapter 68, Collective Bargaining for State Employees (ss. 5-270 to 5-280)
governing_statute.quote: Employees shall have, and shall be protected in the exercise of the right of self-organization, to form, join or assist any employee organization, to bargain collectively through representatives of their own choosing on questions of wages, hours and other conditions of employment

who_may_bargain.value: Any state employee, classified or not, except elected or appointed officials (other than special deputy sheriffs), board and commission members, managerial and confidential employees, and other listed exclusions
who_may_bargain.quote: “Employee” means any employee of an employer, whether or not in the classified service of the employer, except elected or appointed officials other than special deputy sheriffs, board and commission members

impasse_procedure.value: Optional mediation through the State Board of Mediation and Arbitration on joint request, then binding interest arbitration that either party may start by filing the impasse issues with that Board. Agreements and awards go to the General Assembly under s. 5-278.
impasse_procedure.quote: both parties or either of them may initiate arbitration by filing with the State Board of Mediation and Arbitration a list of the issues as to which an impasse has been reached.

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible from nonconsenting public employees under Janus v. AFSCME (2018). The fee requirement for non-members in s. 5-280(a) remains in the statute text.

dfr_forum.value: State Board of Labor Relations. The duty of fair representation is express in s. 5-271(d), and prohibited-practice questions about employee organizations go to the Board under s. 5-274.
dfr_forum.quote: When an employee organization has been designated, in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, as the exclusive representative of employees in an appropriate unit, it shall have a duty of fair representation to the members of that unit.
